title: Native plugin/install mechanism per coding-agent harness (2026) -- revised: OpenCode has no per-tool context-injection hook
body:
Inject OpenCode context only through experimental.chat.system.transform; it has no per-tool-call hook like PreToolUse. Supersedes the OpenCode row of the prior version of this memory (id 23b85e93), which assumed tool.execute.before/session.created/session.idle could carry DD's advisory context the way Claude Code's PreToolUse does. Confirmed false by reading @opencode-ai/plugin@1.18.31's actual .d.ts and a real installed plugin's source (opencode-helicone-session): tool.execute.before's output is {args} only, no text-injection field; event (session lifecycle) returns void, no output object at all. The ONLY OpenCode hook that accepts injectable text is experimental.chat.system.transform: (input:{sessionID?,model}, output:{system:string[]}), firing once per chat turn, not once per tool call -- there is no OpenCode hook shaped like Claude Code's PreToolUse. tool.execute.after's output ({title,output,metadata}) also has no structured exit/error signal, so wiring tool-execution observation there risks misclassifying results rather than skipping them as unknown. The other three rows (Claude Code marketplace, Grok Build marketplace mirroring it almost exactly including auto-discovery of root-level skills/ and .mcp.json, Codex having no marketplace/npm-pull at all) held up under implementation and stay as originally recorded.

Why: Verified 2026-09-19 while implementing adapters/opencode/index.js for docs/plans/2026-09-19-harness-native-install-plan.md Task 4. The first version of this memory was written from doc-summary research only (WebFetch of opencode.ai/docs/plugins/, which described hook *names* but not exact signatures); this revision is from reading the actual published type definitions and a real plugin's compiled source before writing any code, exactly the verification step the plan's own Task 4 Step 1 required.

evidence.summary: Header comment cites the exact @opencode-ai/plugin version and real reference plugin read before writing the shim; the shim itself only wires experimental.chat.system.transform, nothing per-tool.
States the confirmed hook-signature findings and what was/wasn't verified (opencode debug startup ran clean; live mid-conversation firing not verified).
Anchored delivery: keywords validated against this memory's own text and a generic-request corpus before proposing.

v1.trigger: Designing or implementing how DD is installed/distributed into a target project for Claude Code, Grok Build, OpenCode, or Codex.
